newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER SHOWCASE-REAL MADRID AND BETIS IN 2-2 THRILLER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-REAL MADRID AND BETIS IN 2-2 THRILLER.

text.p: Spanish league leaders Real Madrid had to struggle to keep their unbeaten record intact in a thrilling 2-2 draw with third-placed Real Betis on Saturday.

The result leaves Real Madrid nine points clear at the top ahead of Sunday's game between second-placed Barcelona and Racing Santander. Betis, themselves unbeaten away from home, are a further point back, but with a game in hand.
Betis had marginally the better of the match, despite some difficult moments towards the end.

"We're happy with the attitude ... we were brave, we showed personality. It would be wrong to say that we're disappointed with a draw in the Bernabeu stadium," said Betis manager Serra Ferrer afterwards.

Serra Ferrer's side had started at a furious pace, and with just seven minutes on the clock Findi George found space on the right, the defence failed to clear his cross and keeper Bodo Illgner was unable to keep out Alfonso Perez's header.
The visitors could have gone further in front when Croatian international Robert Jarni thumped a free-kick against the post with Illgner completely beaten.
Moments later Predrag Mijatovic returned the favour to clip the bar with a superb chip from the edge of the area.
With Raul Gonazalez having a quiet game down the left, Mijatovic and Davor Suker looked dangerous on the right-flank and put Betis defender Tomas Olias under constant pressure.
And it was from the right that Real Madrid equalised after 20 minutes.
A superb move opened up the Betis defence to leave Emilio Amavisca completely unmarked and Mijatovic had no trouble in knocking in his cross.
Betis came out more strongly after the break, but it was Real Madrid who took the lead when Roberto Carlos lifted a free-kick from the left into the box and Christian Panucci rose to head home.
The former AC Milan defender was booked for celebrating his second goal for his new club by tearing off his shirt and uprooting the corner flag to wave it to the crowd.
Betis fought back to equalise on the hour when Finidi outjumped his former Ajax team mate Clarence Seedorf to make it 2-2 from a Jarni free-kick.

Illgner kept his side in the game with a superb save from Alfonso midway through the second-half, before his opposite number Toni Prats completed a fine performance by tipping a last-minute effort from Brazilian defender Roberto Carlos over the bar.
For a Betis side that already seem almost certain to win a UEFA Cup place, the result was a boost in the bid to displace Barcelona for Spain's second Champions' League berth.
"It will be tough ... but we've shown we can play well away, and we can go to Barcelona with confidence," said striker Alfonso.
